argument_summary: The current record supports only a narrowed, caveated defense of certification. Admissible evidence shows aggregate launch readiness is 2.2 points above threshold, the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the launch is limited to a reversible 6% rollout with monitoring and rollback. That is relevant governance evidence. But the same record also shows the grant compliance review segment remains below target, remains exposed in the initial cohort, and is not covered by an approved risk acceptance that expressly addresses that exposure. The strongest supportable position is that the packet demonstrates meaningful controls and disclosure-oriented governance, not clean satisfaction of the release-policy condition for the exposed use case.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the grant-cycle rollout path, and that cost is real, but business cost does not change the policy standard. The practical implication is narrower: because the record already shows monitored, reversible controls and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, the auditor could avoid treating this as a broad control failure and instead handle it as a bounded policy-gap finding tied to the exposed grant compliance review segment.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy is the specific release-policy rule, not the general public guidance on model cards or deployment monitoring. Under the admissible policy text, rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. On this record, neither condition is satisfied. Public guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring deployment supports the governance framing of the packet, but it does not by itself satisfy the pre-launch policy threshold for an exposed named use case.
concessions: The grant compliance review segment is below target on allowable-cost explanation.
The affected grant compliance review segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by cohort and does not exclude the affected use case.
The only risk acceptance in evidence is a draft with a blank approver line and it does not mention grant compliance review exposure.
General public guidance about disclosure and monitoring does not override the specific pre-launch release policy.
